newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas seen as a favourite to join DAX.
newsitem.headline: Adidas seen as a favourite to join DAX.

text.p: Adidas AG is a favourite to join the German 30-share DAX index and replace struggling retailer Karstadt AG, equity analysts said on Monday.

Adidas, the sportswear firm with the legendary three-stripe logo, is considered a top candidate for the blue-chip index next month because it is among the top 35 German shares in trading volume and market capitalisation, as of end-March.

Adidas ranked 30th in turnover at 15.1 billion marks ($8.7 billion) and had a market capitalisation of 8.34 billion marks. Karstadt, meanwhile, ranked 32nd in turnover at 13.4 billion marks and 40th in market capitalisation at 4.98 billion marks.
Industry analysts also expect Adidas' position to strengthen and Karstadt's to deteriorate in the final ranking done at the end of June. June data would be used as a basis for any DAX changes.
The DAX portfolio will be reviewed by a panel consisting of seven German banks, a newspaper and the German bourse on July 22 to determine if any changes should be made to the DAX.
Any changes take effect on the third Friday of September.

But analysts said the question of whether Adidas, founded in 1920 by Adi Dassler, has been around long enough as a publicly-traded group may be a stumbling point that prompts a panel to put off a decision on changing the DAX until 1998.

"I think it is very likely," said Michael Wand, a retailing analyst at Paribas Capital Markets in London, of Adidas joining the DAX index. "It has all the features needed for the index -- a huge free float and sufficient market capitalisation.
"But the short history of Adidas on the stock market, less than two years, may be a bad factor," Wand said. "They like companies that have a long track record on the stock market."
Still, some analysts see Adidas clearing the hurdle this year, which could drive its stock to record highs because of investors' traditionally strong demand for DAX stocks.

Speculation about Adidas joining the DAX index has been one reason behind the roughly 55-percent rise in Adidas shares this year, which has outpaced a 30-percent rise in the DAX, at a time when other sportswear groups have been suffering.

Karstadt has underperformed the DAX and has risen only about 20 percent this year, suffering from low trading volumes and doubts about management's ability to turn the group around from ongoing troubles, analysts said.
Wand said one important factor favouring Adidas is that it has become a dominant player in the consumer sector, an area under-represented in the DAX index.
"I would say that there is at least a 60 percent chance of Adidas making it into the DAX," said one analyst at a major Frankfurt bank who asked not to be identified.

Adidas' entry into the DAX would be another victory for Robert-Louis Dreyfus, who led a group of international investors that bought Adidas and then, restructured the group before the public offering in November 1995.

But DAX membership can be a political decision as banks on the board push their favourite candidates, sometimes ones in which they hold major stakes since being thrown out of the DAX can often cause a sell-off in a share.
Indeed, Germany's largest commercial bank, Deutsche Bank AG, sits on the board that will make the decision on the DAX make-up on July 22 and has a 10 percent stake in Karstadt.
"With this commission, you never know what can happen," said one industry analyst. "But Adidas is a good fit for the DAX and will certainly make it into the DAX sometime soon."
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
($ = 1.729 German Marks)
